items.stem: You copy a formula down a column, but one cell reference must always point to the same tax-rate cell. What should you use?

options.rationale: Correct: locking the reference with $ keeps it fixed when copied.

options.text: A relative reference such as B1
options.rationale: A relative reference shifts as the formula is copied.

options.text: A new formula typed in every row

options.rationale: Merging cells does not fix a reference.

items.explanation: Correct: locking the reference with $ keeps it fixed when copied.

items.stem: Which TWO tools help summarize a large table in Google Sheets? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: pivot tables aggregate data by category.

options.text: A chart built on the summary
options.rationale: Correct: a chart visualizes the summarized data.

options.text: Manually retyping totals into a note
options.rationale: Manual totals are error-prone and not dynamic.

options.text: Deleting rows until only totals remain
options.rationale: Deleting source data destroys the detail.

items.explanation: Correct: pivot tables and charts summarize and visualize data.

items.stem: Which function totals only the values that meet a condition?

options.rationale: Correct: SUMIF totals values matching a criterion.
COUNT counts numeric cells; it does not total by condition.
TRIM removes extra spaces from text.
